purpose: Separate full-roster registration, concurrent provider initialization, session activation, task claiming, and durable result delivery.

architecture.registration: Every configured actor is committed at controller startup, including actors whose native session is not ready.
architecture.initialization: Controller and native Codex protocol host no longer wait for all terminal session bindings. Quiet-generation special casing and all-terminal backend-restart preflight were removed.
architecture.activation: herdr_activation.rs validates project/namespace generation, process lifetime and expected recovered session before opening each terminal's execution gate. Runtime evidence is separate from logical configuration; activation does not reload or replace providers.
architecture.execution: Queue admission is durable while a target is not ready. Task claiming and reattaching terminal work require that target's verified binding. Unknown prior launch effects are not automatically resent.
architecture.delivery: Result addressing and inbox observation use registration rather than dispatch permission. Results remain durable for offline or disabled recipients; normal mailbox processing wakes an eligible recipient.
architecture.recovery: Missing native evidence holds that actor and preserves its work. Prior confirmed identity remains usable for workspace ownership checks, without authorizing execution or creating fresh history.

changes_removed: binding-driven subset registration and startup reload

original_red.meaning: Previous quiet-only implementation did not start Codex while a recovering Pi with queued work remained unready.

broad_startup.resolution: The ACK-loss fixture now waits for both parallel launches to take effect before killing the opener. Corrected case passed in final acceptance; uncertain unsent launch remains non-replayable.

resolutions: Two wrong-session fixtures stopped on null error-field polling; corrected refusal tests passed in native-lifecycle-separation-final-session-fences-20261014.xml.
Missing-history recovery now preserves last known identity for ownership while retaining an execution hold; passed final acceptance.
Migration fixture changed executable directory and therefore injected PATH. Corrected in-place replacement passed without weakening configuration comparison.

validation.limits: Controlled Windows process/IPC fault-injection tests, fixture Herdr/Pi/Claude terminals, and real installed Codex app-server initialization with private unauthenticated homes. No new live three-model business workflow or production startup benchmark was run.

delivery.reason: Existing sample-project-3 installation processes are still active; no approval to stop and restore that project has been received.

remaining_limits: Mixed-version Codex model-catalog cache churn is unchanged.
Ambiguous launch outcome or missing/corrupt session evidence remains an explicit per-actor hold, never a silent reset or blind task replay.
